A hospital runs a shared pool of operating rooms managed by two independent
scheduling coordinators. Because the surgical theatre is periodically
reconfigured, the system tracks a monotone epoch number that advances on every
reconfiguration. Each coordinator remembers the epoch it last synchronised to.
When a coordinator reconfigures the theatre it advances the global epoch and
adopts the new value locally. A coordinator whose local epoch has fallen behind
must first synchronise before it may act again. Only a coordinator synchronised
to the current epoch is authorised to book a free room or release a room it
already holds, and each booking records the epoch under which it was made.
This prevents a stale coordinator from interfering with the shared pool.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every booked operating room carries a positive booking epoch that never exceeds the current global epoch, so no stale or unauthorised coordinator can have recorded it.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m9p6t3 --------------------------
\* Multiplayer game lobby matchmaker. Matchmaking rounds are numbered by a
\* monotone epoch. When the matchmaker rotates the lobby the epoch advances and
\* it emits fresh invites stamped with the new epoch. Invites travel through the
\* network and may be delivered late -- a player can be slow, but is never lost:
\* every in-flight invite is eventually delivered. A player may take a seat in a
\* match only while holding a ticket stamped with the CURRENT lobby epoch, so a
\* slow player carrying a stale ticket is not authorised to be seated.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Matches, MaxEpoch, None

\* lobbyEpoch: current round; ticket[p]: epoch of p's last delivered invite;
\* seat[p]: match p sits in or None; seatEpoch[p]: epoch p was seated under;
\* inflight: set of undelivered invites, each [p |-> player, e |-> epoch].
VARIABLES lobbyEpoch, ticket, seat, seatEpoch, inflight

vars == <<lobbyEpoch, ticket, seat, seatEpoch, inflight>>

Invite(p, e) == [p |-> p, e |-> e]

TypeOK ==
    /\ lobbyEpoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ ticket \in [Players -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ seat \in [Players -> Matches \cup {None}]
    /\ seatEpoch \in [Players -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ inflight \subseteq {Invite(p, e) : p \in Players, e \in 0..MaxEpoch}

Init ==
    /\ lobbyEpoch = 1
    /\ ticket = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ seat = [p \in Players |-> None]
    /\ seatEpoch = [p \in Players |-> 0]
    /\ inflight = {}

\* Rotate the lobby into a new matchmaking round.
Rotate ==
    /\ lobbyEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ lobbyEpoch' = lobbyEpoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ticket, seat, seatEpoch, inflight>>

\* Emit an invite for a player who has none outstanding.
SendInvite(p) ==
    /\ \A m \in inflight : m.p # p
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {Invite(p, lobbyEpoch)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyEpoch, ticket, seat, seatEpoch>>

\* Deliver a delayed invite -- possibly long after its epoch has passed.
Deliver(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflight
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![m.p] = m.e]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyEpoch, seat, seatEpoch>>

\* Seat a player only while its delivered ticket matches the current epoch.
Seat(p, k) ==
    /\ ticket[p] = lobbyEpoch
    /\ seat[p] = None
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = k]
    /\ seatEpoch' = [seatEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = lobbyEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyEpoch, ticket, inflight>>

\* A seated player leaves the match.
Leave(p) ==
    /\ seat[p] # None
    /\ seat' = [seat EXCEPT ![p] = None]
    /\ seatEpoch' = [seatEpoch EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lobbyEpoch, ticket, inflight>>

Next ==
    \/ Rotate
    \/ \E p \in Players : SendInvite(p)
    \/ \E m \in inflight : Deliver(m)
    \/ \E p \in Players, k \in Matches : Seat(p, k)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Leave(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A player occupies a seat exactly when it carries a positive seating stamp,
\* and that stamp never runs ahead of the lobby: the seat record and the epoch
\* stamp move together, so no unauthorised (unstamped) seating can exist.
AuthorizedSeating ==
    \A p \in Players :
        /\ (seat[p] # None) <=> (seatEpoch[p] # 0)
        /\ seatEpoch[p] <= lobbyEpoch
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {p1, p2}
    Matches = {m1, m2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthorizedSeating
CONSTRAINT TypeOK
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby uses a matchmaker to seat players into matches.
Matchmaking proceeds in numbered rounds tracked by a monotone epoch. Whenever
the matchmaker rotates the lobby the epoch advances by one. The matchmaker
sends each waiting player an invite stamped with the current epoch, and a
player may have at most one invite outstanding at a time. Invites travel over
the network and can be delivered late, modelling a player that is slow but
never failed: every in-flight invite eventually arrives and updates that
player's ticket. A player may take a seat in a match only while its most
recently delivered ticket carries the current lobby epoch, and each seating
records the epoch under which it happened. A seated player may later leave,
clearing its seat and stamp together.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A player holds a seat exactly when it carries a positive seating stamp, and that stamp never exceeds the current lobby epoch, so no stale player is ever recorded as seated without current authorisation.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m8p0t5 --------------------------
\* Stock-exchange opening auction. Each order book is a critical resource whose
\* matching engine must run under mutual exclusion. Access is protected by a
\* two-level (hierarchical) lock: a trader must first hold the coarse session
\* lock before it may take the fine per-book lock, and only the holder of a
\* book's fine lock may run that book's opening match. A privileged exchange
\* admin may forcibly seize any fine lock to intervene, without disturbing the
\* mutual-exclusion discipline.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Traders, Books, Admin, None

\* coarse: holder of the coarse session lock or None; fine[b]: holder of book
\* b's fine lock or None; matched[b]: whether b's opening auction has matched;
\* overridden: the set of books the admin has forcibly seized.
VARIABLES coarse, fine, matched, overridden

vars == <<coarse, fine, matched, overridden>>

Actors == Traders \cup {Admin}

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Traders \cup {None}
    /\ fine \in [Books -> Actors \cup {None}]
    /\ matched \in [Books -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ overridden \subseteq Books

Init ==
    /\ coarse = None
    /\ fine = [b \in Books |-> None]
    /\ matched = [b \in Books |-> FALSE]
    /\ overridden = {}

\* Take the coarse session lock when it is free.
AcquireCoarse(t) ==
    /\ coarse = None
    /\ coarse' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, matched, overridden>>

\* Take a book's fine lock -- only permitted to the coarse-lock holder.
AcquireFine(t, b) ==
    /\ coarse = t
    /\ fine[b] = None
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, matched, overridden>>

\* Run a book's opening match under its fine lock.
MatchBook(t, b) ==
    /\ fine[b] = t
    /\ matched[b] = FALSE
    /\ matched' = [matched EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, overridden>>

\* Release a fine lock held by the actor.
ReleaseFine(t, b) ==
    /\ fine[b] = t
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, matched, overridden>>

\* Release the coarse lock, permitted only once no fine lock is still held.
ReleaseCoarse(t) ==
    /\ coarse = t
    /\ \A b \in Books : fine[b] # t
    /\ coarse' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, matched, overridden>>

\* Privileged admin override: forcibly seize a book's fine lock, once per book.
AdminOverride(b) ==
    /\ b \notin overridden
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = Admin]
    /\ overridden' = overridden \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, matched>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : AcquireCoarse(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders, b \in Books : AcquireFine(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Actors, b \in Books : MatchBook(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Actors, b \in Books : ReleaseFine(t, b)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : ReleaseCoarse(t)
    \/ \E b \in Books : AdminOverride(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StateBound == Cardinality(overridden) <= Cardinality(Books)

\* Every held fine lock belongs either to the single current coarse-lock holder
\* or to the privileged admin. Since at most one trader holds the coarse lock,
\* no two competing traders can hold fine locks at once: mutual exclusion of the
\* critical order-book resource is enforced by the lock hierarchy.
LockHierarchy ==
    \A b \in Books :
        fine[b] # None => (fine[b] = coarse \/ fine[b] = Admin)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Traders = {t1, t2}
    Books = {b1, b2}
    Admin = Admin
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LockHierarchy
CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
A stock exchange opens each trading day by running an opening auction over its
order books. Each order book is a critical resource whose matching engine must
run under mutual exclusion. The exchange protects books with a two-level lock
hierarchy: a trader must first acquire the single coarse session lock, and only
then may it take the fine per-book lock. Only the holder of a book's fine lock
may run that book's opening match. A trader may release the coarse lock only
after it has released every fine lock it held. A privileged exchange admin may
forcibly seize any book's fine lock to intervene during the auction. Because
only one trader can hold the coarse lock at a time, and fine locks are reserved
for that holder or the admin, competing traders can never run a book
concurrently.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every held fine per-book lock belongs either to the single current coarse-lock holder or to the privileged admin, so no two competing traders ever hold a book's critical lock at the same time.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m1p4t2 --------------------------
\* Smart-home door-lock network. Two controllers share one pool of door locks
\* and are arranged in a token ring: a single access token circulates around the
\* ring, and only the controller currently holding the token may unlock or
\* relock a door. The token is handed on by an in-flight pass message, so while
\* it is in transit no controller holds it. The network has a bounded capacity
\* of simultaneously unlocked doors (for safety, only so many doors may stand
\* open at once), and a controller may open a new door only while capacity
\* remains.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Doors, Capacity, None

N == Cardinality(Nodes)
Succ(n) == (n + 1) % N

\* token: controller holding the token, or None while in transit; transit: the
\* set of destinations the token is being passed to (empty or a singleton);
\* unlocked: the set of doors currently open; opener[d]: controller that opened
\* door d, or None.
VARIABLES token, transit, unlocked, opener

vars == <<token, transit, unlocked, opener>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Nodes \cup {None}
    /\ transit \subseteq Nodes
    /\ unlocked \subseteq Doors
    /\ opener \in [Doors -> Nodes \cup {None}]

Init ==
    /\ token = 0
    /\ transit = {}
    /\ unlocked = {}
    /\ opener = [d \in Doors |-> None]

\* The token holder releases the token toward its ring successor.
StartPass(n) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ transit' = {Succ(n)}
    /\ token' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unlocked, opener>>

\* An in-flight token is delivered to its destination controller.
DeliverToken(m) ==
    /\ token = None
    /\ m \in transit
    /\ token' = m
    /\ transit' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<unlocked, opener>>

\* The token holder opens a door, but only while capacity remains.
Unlock(n, d) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ d \notin unlocked
    /\ Cardinality(unlocked) < Capacity
    /\ unlocked' = unlocked \cup {d}
    /\ opener' = [opener EXCEPT ![d] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, transit>>

\* The token holder relocks a door it opened.
Relock(n, d) ==
    /\ token = n
    /\ d \in unlocked
    /\ opener[d] = n
    /\ unlocked' = unlocked \ {d}
    /\ opener' = [opener EXCEPT ![d] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, transit>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : StartPass(n)
    \/ \E m \in Nodes : DeliverToken(m)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, d \in Doors : Unlock(n, d)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, d \in Doors : Relock(n, d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The number of simultaneously unlocked doors never exceeds the configured
\* capacity of the network.
CapacityRespected == Cardinality(unlocked) <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {0, 1}
    Doors = {d1, d2, d3}
    Capacity = 2
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
CONSTRAINT TypeOK
nl:
A smart-home system manages a network of door locks shared by two independent
controllers. The controllers are arranged in a token ring: a single access
token circulates around the ring, and only the controller currently holding the
token is allowed to act on the shared pool of doors. When the holder wants to
hand the token on, it releases it as an in-flight pass message addressed to its
ring successor, and while the token is in transit no controller holds it. When
the message is delivered, the destination controller becomes the new holder.
The token holder may unlock a closed door only while the network is below its
bounded capacity of simultaneously open doors, and it may relock any door it
opened. This keeps the number of open doors within the configured safety limit.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of simultaneously unlocked doors never exceeds the configured bounded capacity of the network.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m3p5t1 --------------------------
\* Car-wash conveyor line. Each car reaching the end of the line receives a
\* final protective wax seal -- an irreversible action that must be applied at
\* most once per car. Control of the line is held by an elected leader; on
\* failover a new leader is elected with a strictly higher term. Only the
\* current leader's finalize command may seal a car. Finalize commands travel
\* through the controller network and may be reordered, so a command carrying an
\* old (superseded) term can arrive late and must be discarded rather than
\* applied.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Cars, MaxTerm, None

\* term: highest election term so far; leader: current leader node or None;
\* done[c]: whether car c has received its irreversible seal; sealedBy[c]: the
\* leader node that sealed c, or None; sealTerm[c]: the term c was sealed under
\* (0 if unsealed); msgs: the set of in-flight finalize commands (reorderable).
VARIABLES term, leader, done, sealedBy, sealTerm, msgs

vars == <<term, leader, done, sealedBy, sealTerm, msgs>>

Cmd(c, t) == [car |-> c, trm |-> t]

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {None}
    /\ done \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ sealedBy \in [Cars -> Nodes \cup {None}]
    /\ sealTerm \in [Cars -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ msgs \subseteq {Cmd(c, t) : c \in Cars, t \in 0..MaxTerm}

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = None
    /\ done = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]
    /\ sealedBy = [c \in Cars |-> None]
    /\ sealTerm = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ msgs = {}

\* Failover: elect a new leader under a strictly higher term.
Elect(n) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, sealedBy, sealTerm, msgs>>

\* The current leader issues (or re-issues) a finalize command for a car.
Emit(c) ==
    /\ leader # None
    /\ msgs' = msgs \cup {Cmd(c, term)}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, done, sealedBy, sealTerm>>

\* Apply a finalize command -- only if it carries the current term and the car
\* is still unsealed, so the irreversible seal happens at most once.
Apply(m) ==
    /\ m \in msgs
    /\ leader # None
    /\ m.trm = term
    /\ done[m.car] = FALSE
    /\ done' = [done EXCEPT ![m.car] = TRUE]
    /\ sealedBy' = [sealedBy EXCEPT ![m.car] = leader]
    /\ sealTerm' = [sealTerm EXCEPT ![m.car] = term]
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader>>

\* Discard a reordered command carrying a superseded (stale) term.
Discard(m) ==
    /\ m \in msgs
    /\ m.trm < term
    /\ msgs' = msgs \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, done, sealedBy, sealTerm>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Emit(c)
    \/ \E m \in msgs : Apply(m)
    \/ \E m \in msgs : Discard(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StateBound == term <= MaxTerm

\* Every car that has received its one irreversible seal is attributed to a real
\* leader node and stamped with a positive term that never exceeds the current
\* term. The seal is a single recorded event tied to the leader that applied it.
OneShotSeal ==
    \A c \in Cars :
        done[c] =>
            /\ sealedBy[c] \in Nodes
            /\ 0 < sealTerm[c]
            /\ sealTerm[c] <= term
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2}
    Cars = {ca, cb}
    MaxTerm = 3
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OneShotSeal
CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line applies a final protective wax seal to each car as it
reaches the end of the line. That seal is irreversible and must be applied at
most once per car. The line is run by a single controller elected as leader;
when a controller fails, a new leader is elected under a strictly higher term.
Only the current leader may issue a finalize command, each stamped with the
leader's term, and it may re-issue commands for a car. Commands travel through the controller network
and can be reordered, so a command stamped with an old, superseded term may
arrive late. A late command carrying a stale term is discarded, while a command
carrying the current term seals a car only if that car has not already been
sealed. Each seal records the leader and term that applied it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every car that has received its irreversible seal is attributed to exactly one real leader node and stamped with a positive term not exceeding the current term, so the seal is applied at most once.

spec_text:
-------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m9p2t2 --------------------------
\* Subway signalling block system. A fixed number of movement authorities (the
\* permissions that let a train enter a track block) is distributed across the
\* blocks and is neither created nor destroyed -- authorities are only moved.
\* Two independent signalling coordinators share this single pool. Because the
\* signalling plan is periodically reconfigured, a monotone epoch is tracked;
\* each coordinator carries the epoch it last adopted, and only a coordinator on
\* the current epoch may dispatch an authority into transit or land one into a
\* block. At every moment the authorities resident in blocks plus those in
\* transit sum to the fixed total.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Coords, Blocks, Total, MaxEpoch, None

\* epoch: current reconfiguration epoch; local[c]: epoch coordinator c adopted;
\* held[b]: authorities resident in block b; moving: authorities in transit.
VARIABLES epoch, local, held, moving

vars == <<epoch, local, held, moving>>

Authorized(c) == local[c] = epoch

RECURSIVE SumHeld(_)
SumHeld(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN held[b] + SumHeld(S \ {b})

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ local \in [Coords -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ held \in [Blocks -> 0..Total]
    /\ moving \in 0..Total

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ local = [c \in Coords |-> 0]
    /\ held = [b \in Blocks |-> IF b = CHOOSE x \in Blocks : TRUE THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ moving = 0

\* Reconfigure the signalling plan: advance the epoch and adopt it locally.
Reconfigure(c) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ local' = [local EXCEPT ![c] = epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, moving>>

\* A lagging coordinator adopts the current epoch.
Sync(c) ==
    /\ local[c] < epoch
    /\ local' = [local EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, held, moving>>

\* An authorised coordinator dispatches one authority from a block into transit.
Dispatch(c, b) ==
    /\ Authorized(c)
    /\ held[b] > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = held[b] - 1]
    /\ moving' = moving + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, local>>

\* An authorised coordinator lands an in-transit authority into a block.
Arrive(c, b) ==
    /\ Authorized(c)
    /\ moving > 0
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = held[b] + 1]
    /\ moving' = moving - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, local>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Coords : Reconfigure(c)
    \/ \E c \in Coords : Sync(c)
    \/ \E c \in Coords, b \in Blocks : Dispatch(c, b)
    \/ \E c \in Coords, b \in Blocks : Arrive(c, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

StateBound == epoch <= MaxEpoch

\* Conservation: the authorities resident in blocks plus those in transit always
\* sum to the fixed total, and no bucket is ever negative -- nothing is created
\* or destroyed, only moved.
Conservation ==
    /\ moving >= 0
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : held[b] >= 0
    /\ SumHeld(Blocks) + moving = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Coords = {c1, c2}
    Blocks = {x1, x2}
    Total = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
CONSTRAINT StateBound
nl:
A subway signalling system controls train movement through track blocks using a
fixed pool of movement authorities. An authority is the permission that lets a
train enter a block, and the total number of authorities is fixed: they are
only ever moved between blocks, never created or destroyed. Two independent
signalling coordinators share this single pool. Because the signalling plan is
periodically reconfigured, the system tracks a monotone epoch, and each
coordinator carries the epoch it last adopted. A coordinator that has fallen
behind must synchronise before acting. Only a coordinator on the current epoch
may dispatch an authority out of a block into transit, or land an in-transit
authority into a block. At all times the authorities resident in blocks plus
those in transit account for exactly the fixed total.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The authorities resident in the blocks plus those currently in transit always sum to the fixed total and no bucket is ever negative, so nothing is created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m1p6t5 ----
\* Subway signalling block system. A single movement authority (the "token")
\* circulates among trains as in-flight grant messages tagged with an epoch.
\* Only the current token holder may enter a signalling block, and a grant
\* message from an older epoch is stale and must be rejected on delivery.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, None, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES token, epoch, inflight, entered, authEpoch
vars == <<token, epoch, inflight, entered, authEpoch>>

\* A grant message names the intended recipient and the epoch it was minted in.
Grant == [to : Trains, ep : 0 .. MaxEpoch]

EpochBound == epoch <= MaxEpoch

Init ==
  /\ token \in Trains
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ inflight = {}
  /\ entered = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
  /\ authEpoch = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]

\* The holder relinquishes the token by minting a fresh grant to another train.
PassToken(t, u) ==
  /\ token = t
  /\ u # t
  /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {[to |-> u, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ token' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, entered, authEpoch>>

\* A grant minted in the current epoch is honoured; the recipient gets the token.
DeliverFresh(m) ==
  /\ token = None
  /\ m.ep = epoch
  /\ token' = m.to
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, entered, authEpoch>>

\* A grant from an older epoch is stale: it is discarded, granting nobody.
DropStale(m) ==
  /\ m.ep < epoch
  /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, epoch, entered, authEpoch>>

\* Only the token holder may occupy a free block, stamping the current epoch.
EnterBlock(t, b) ==
  /\ token = t
  /\ entered[b] = None
  /\ entered' = [entered EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ authEpoch' = [authEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, epoch, inflight>>

\* Signalling reconfiguration bumps the epoch and clears every block; any train
\* still standing is ejected so no occupant can survive under a stale authority.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ entered' = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
  /\ authEpoch' = [b \in Blocks |-> epoch + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, inflight>>

\* Privileged control-centre override: force the token to a chosen train.
AdminGrant(u) ==
  /\ token' = u
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inflight, entered, authEpoch>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, u \in Trains : PassToken(t, u)
  \/ \E m \in inflight : DeliverFresh(m)
  \/ \E m \in inflight : DropStale(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : EnterBlock(t, b)
  \/ Reconfigure
  \/ \E u \in Trains : AdminGrant(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every occupied block was authorised under the epoch that is current now:
\* no train remains in a block on the strength of a superseded authority.
NoStaleOccupancy ==
  \A b \in Blocks : entered[b] # None => authEpoch[b] = epoch
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  Blocks = {b1, b2}
  None = None
  MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleOccupancy
CONSTRAINT EpochBound
nl:
A subway signalling system controls which trains may enter track blocks. At any
moment a single movement authority, called the token, belongs to one train, or
is temporarily in transit as a grant message. Each grant message names the train
it is meant for and carries the epoch number that was current when it was minted.
The train currently holding the token can hand it off by minting a fresh grant to
another train, after which it holds the token no longer. When a grant is
delivered, it is honoured only if its epoch matches the current epoch; a grant
left over from an earlier epoch is stale and is simply discarded, granting the
token to nobody. Only the train that holds the token may move into a free block,
and its occupancy is stamped with the epoch that was current at entry. The
signalling centre can reconfigure the line, which advances the epoch and clears
every block so that no train keeps a block under an authority that has since been
superseded. A privileged control-centre override may additionally force the token
to any chosen train.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no train ever remains inside a block on the strength of a stale authority; every occupied block was authorised under the epoch that is current now.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m8p3t3 ----
\* Print-shop job spooler with two-level (hierarchical) locking. A job must
\* first take the COARSE lock of a printer, and only then may it take a FINE
\* lock on an individual output slot. A job may be slow -- it can mark itself
\* delayed and linger holding its coarse lock -- but it is never failed; it
\* always eventually resumes.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Jobs, Printers, Slots, None

VARIABLES coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase, waiting
vars == <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase, waiting>>

Init ==
  /\ coarseOwner = [p \in Printers |-> None]
  /\ fineOwner = [s \in Slots |-> None]
  /\ jobSlot = [j \in Jobs |-> None]
  /\ jobPrinter = [j \in Jobs |-> None]
  /\ phase = [j \in Jobs |-> "idle"]
  /\ waiting = [j \in Jobs |-> FALSE]

\* Level 1: take the coarse lock of a free printer. Required before any slot.
AcquireCoarse(j, p) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "idle"
  /\ coarseOwner[p] = None
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![p] = j]
  /\ jobPrinter' = [jobPrinter EXCEPT ![j] = p]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, jobSlot, waiting>>

\* Level 2: only a job already holding a coarse lock, and not currently
\* delayed, may claim a free fine slot; the claim is recorded on both sides.
AcquireFine(j, s) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ ~waiting[j]
  /\ fineOwner[s] = None
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![s] = j]
  /\ jobSlot' = [jobSlot EXCEPT ![j] = s]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "fine"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, jobPrinter, waiting>>

\* Release the fine slot (finish printing that slot), keeping the coarse lock.
ReleaseFine(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "fine"
  /\ fineOwner' = [fineOwner EXCEPT ![jobSlot[j]] = None]
  /\ jobSlot' = [jobSlot EXCEPT ![j] = None]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "coarse"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, jobPrinter, waiting>>

\* Release the coarse lock once no fine slot is held, freeing the printer.
ReleaseCoarse(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ jobSlot[j] = None
  /\ coarseOwner' = [coarseOwner EXCEPT ![jobPrinter[j]] = None]
  /\ jobPrinter' = [jobPrinter EXCEPT ![j] = None]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![j] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, jobSlot, waiting>>

\* The job is slow: it marks itself delayed while still holding its coarse lock.
SlowWait(j) ==
  /\ phase[j] = "coarse"
  /\ ~waiting[j]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![j] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase>>

\* A slow job is not a failed job: it always eventually resumes.
Resume(j) ==
  /\ waiting[j]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![j] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, jobSlot, jobPrinter, phase>>

Next ==
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, p \in Printers : AcquireCoarse(j, p)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : AcquireFine(j, s)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReleaseFine(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : ReleaseCoarse(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : SlowWait(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : Resume(j)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The slot ledger and the per-job record are mutually consistent inverses:
\* a slot's recorded owner claims exactly that slot, and a job's claimed slot
\* records exactly that job. No slot can therefore be handed to two jobs.
ConsistentSlotOwnership ==
  /\ \A s \in Slots : fineOwner[s] # None => jobSlot[fineOwner[s]] = s
  /\ \A j \in Jobs : jobSlot[j] # None => fineOwner[jobSlot[j]] = j
====
nl:
A print shop runs a job spooler that hands out two kinds of locks in a strict
order. Each printer has one coarse lock, and each output slot has one fine lock.
A job that is idle may first take the coarse lock of a free printer, recording
which printer it now holds. Only a job that already holds a coarse lock, and that
is not currently delayed, may then claim a free fine slot; the claim is written
both into the slot's owner record and into the job's own record of which slot it
holds. A job finishes a slot by releasing its fine lock while keeping its coarse
lock, and later releases the coarse lock once it holds no slot, freeing the
printer. A job may be slow: it can mark itself delayed while still holding its
coarse lock, and a delayed job cannot grab a fine slot until it resumes. A slow
job is never a failed job, because it always eventually resumes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the same output slot is never allocated to two different jobs at once; the slot's owner record and each job's own slot record always agree as exact inverses.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m1p5t4 ----
\* Subway signalling with a circulating movement token. Only the train holding
\* the token acts. The distinctive event here is SEALING a block for permanent
\* single-direction running: sealing is irreversible -- a sealed block is never
\* unsealed -- and the number of sealed blocks is capped by a running capacity
\* that the control centre may raise or lower on the fly.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, None, MaxCap

VARIABLES holder, passes, sealed, sealer, capacity
vars == <<holder, passes, sealed, sealer, capacity>>

CapBound == capacity <= MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ holder \in Trains
  /\ passes = {}
  /\ sealed = {}
  /\ sealer = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
  /\ capacity = 1

\* The token holder releases the token as an in-flight pass to another train.
Circulate(t, u) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ u # t
  /\ passes' = passes \cup {[to |-> u]}
  /\ holder' = None
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealer, capacity>>

\* An in-flight pass is delivered in any order, making its target the holder.
DeliverPass(m) ==
  /\ holder = None
  /\ holder' = m.to
  /\ passes' = passes \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<sealed, sealer, capacity>>

\* The irreversible action: the holder seals an as-yet-unsealed block, provided
\* the number already sealed is below the running capacity. A sealed block is
\* recorded with the train that sealed it and is never unsealed.
Seal(t, b) ==
  /\ holder = t
  /\ b \notin sealed
  /\ Cardinality(sealed) < capacity
  /\ sealed' = sealed \cup {b}
  /\ sealer' = [sealer EXCEPT ![b] = t]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, passes, capacity>>

\* The control centre may raise the running capacity up to the fixed maximum.
RaiseCapacity ==
  /\ capacity < MaxCap
  /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, passes, sealed, sealer>>

\* It may also lower capacity, but never below the count already sealed -- that
\* would demand un-sealing, which the one-way discipline forbids.
LowerCapacity ==
  /\ capacity - 1 >= Cardinality(sealed)
  /\ capacity > 0
  /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, passes, sealed, sealer>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains, u \in Trains : Circulate(t, u)
  \/ \E m \in passes : DeliverPass(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains, b \in Blocks : Seal(t, b)
  \/ RaiseCapacity
  \/ LowerCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A block counts as sealed exactly when it carries a sealer of record, and the
\* sealed count never exceeds the running capacity. Because no action removes a
\* block from the sealed set or clears its sealer, each block is sealed -- the
\* irreversible act -- at most once.
SealIntegrity ==
  /\ \A b \in Blocks : (b \in sealed) <=> (sealer[b] # None)
  /\ Cardinality(sealed) <= capacity
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Trains = {t1, t2}
  Blocks = {b1, b2}
  None = None
  MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SealIntegrity
CONSTRAINT CapBound
nl:
A subway line is coordinated by a single movement token that circulates among
trains; only the train currently holding the token may act. The holder can
release the token as an in-flight pass addressed to another train, and passes are
delivered in any order, at which point the addressed train becomes the new
holder. The special operation on this line is sealing a block for permanent
one-way running. Only the token holder may seal a block, only if that block is
not already sealed, and only while the number of blocks sealed so far is below
the current running capacity; sealing records which train sealed the block. A
sealed block is never unsealed. The control centre may raise the running capacity
up to a fixed maximum, and may lower it at any time, but never below the number
of blocks already sealed, since lowering that far would require undoing a seal.
SAFETY PROPERTY: sealing a block is irreversible and happens at most once per block -- a block carries a sealer of record exactly when it is sealed, and the number of sealed blocks never exceeds the running capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m9p2t1 ----
\* An elevator bank in a skyscraper. A fixed fleet of cars is distributed among
\* shafts, a maintenance bay, and in-flight relocations. Relocations travel as
\* messages that may be delivered in any order. An epoch counter tracks bank
\* reconfigurations; a relocation minted under an older epoch is stale and its
\* car is returned to its origin shaft rather than delivered. Throughout, the
\* fleet is conserved: no car is ever created or destroyed.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Shafts, None, TotalCars, MaxEpoch, MaxId

VARIABLES loc, transit, epoch, parked, nextId
vars == <<loc, transit, epoch, parked, nextId>>

\* Sum of cars parked in the shafts (indistinguishable cars, counted per shaft).
RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

Bounds == nextId <= MaxId /\ epoch <= MaxEpoch

Init ==
  /\ loc \in {f \in [Shafts -> 0 .. TotalCars] : SumOver(f, Shafts) = TotalCars}
  /\ transit = {}
  /\ epoch = 0
  /\ parked = 0
  /\ nextId = 0

\* Send a car from shaft s toward shaft d as an in-flight relocation message.
Dispatch(s, d) ==
  /\ nextId < MaxId
  /\ loc[s] > 0
  /\ d # s
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
  /\ transit' = transit \cup {[id |-> nextId, orig |-> s, dest |-> d, ep |-> epoch]}
  /\ nextId' = nextId + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, parked>>

\* A relocation minted under the current epoch is delivered to its destination.
Arrive(m) ==
  /\ m.ep = epoch
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![m.dest] = @ + 1]
  /\ transit' = transit \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, parked, nextId>>

\* A stale relocation (older epoch) is rejected; its car is returned to origin.
RejectStale(m) ==
  /\ m.ep < epoch
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![m.orig] = @ + 1]
  /\ transit' = transit \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, parked, nextId>>

\* Move a car from a shaft into the maintenance bay.
Park(s) ==
  /\ loc[s] > 0
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
  /\ parked' = parked + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<transit, epoch, nextId>>

\* Return a car from the maintenance bay to a shaft.
Unpark(s) ==
  /\ parked > 0
  /\ loc' = [loc EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
  /\ parked' = parked - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<transit, epoch, nextId>>

\* Reconfigure the bank: advance the epoch. In-flight cars are unaffected in
\* number; older relocations simply become stale.
Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<loc, transit, parked, nextId>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Shafts, d \in Shafts : Dispatch(s, d)
  \/ \E m \in transit : Arrive(m)
  \/ \E m \in transit : RejectStale(m)
  \/ \E s \in Shafts : Park(s)
  \/ \E s \in Shafts : Unpark(s)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Conservation: the cars standing in shafts, the cars in flight, and the cars
\* in the maintenance bay always add up to the full fleet -- nothing created,
\* nothing destroyed.
Conservation == SumOver(loc, Shafts) + Cardinality(transit) + parked = TotalCars
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Shafts = {s1, s2}
  None = None
  TotalCars = 2
  MaxEpoch = 2
  MaxId = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT Conservation
CONSTRAINT Bounds
nl:
A skyscraper elevator bank manages a fixed fleet of cars. At any time each car is
either standing in one of the shafts, riding in the maintenance bay, or in flight
as a relocation being moved from one shaft to another. A relocation is sent by
taking a car out of a shaft and creating an in-flight message that names the
origin shaft, the destination shaft, and the epoch that was current when it was
sent. In-flight relocations may be delivered in any order. When a relocation
minted under the current epoch is delivered, its car is placed into the
destination shaft. When a relocation left over from an older epoch is handled, it
is rejected as stale and its car is returned to its origin shaft instead. A car
may also be moved from a shaft into the maintenance bay and later returned to a
shaft. Reconfiguring the bank advances the epoch, which does not change how many
cars exist but makes older relocations stale.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the fleet is conserved -- the cars standing in shafts, the cars in flight, and the cars in the maintenance bay always sum to exactly the full fleet, so no car is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m2p1t4 ----
\* An air-traffic runway allocator commits allocations to a shared record using
\* two-phase commit. A coordinator proposes an allocation write and asks the
\* control sectors to vote; it commits only if every sector votes yes, otherwise
\* it aborts. A committed write is appended to the shared record and logged as
\* acknowledged, and no acknowledged write is ever dropped from the record. The
\* number of runways available (capacity) can change at runtime but never falls
\* below the number of allocations already committed.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Sectors, Writes, None, MaxCap

VARIABLES phase, votes, pending, record, committedLog, capacity
vars == <<phase, votes, pending, record, committedLog, capacity>>

CapConstraint == capacity <= MaxCap

Init ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ votes = [p \in Sectors |-> "none"]
  /\ pending = None
  /\ record = {}
  /\ committedLog = {}
  /\ capacity = 1

\* Coordinator opens a transaction: proposes a write and asks sectors to vote.
Propose(w) ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ w \notin record
  /\ pending' = w
  /\ phase' = "preparing"
  /\ votes' = [p \in Sectors |-> "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committedLog, capacity>>

\* A sector casts its vote; a yes is only permitted while a runway remains free.
Vote(p, v) ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ votes[p] = "none"
  /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
  /\ (v = "yes") => (Cardinality(record) < capacity)
  /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = v]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, pending, record, committedLog, capacity>>

\* Commit fires only when every sector has voted yes: the write is appended to
\* the shared record and logged as an acknowledged commit.
Commit ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ \A p \in Sectors : votes[p] = "yes"
  /\ record' = record \cup {pending}
  /\ committedLog' = committedLog \cup {pending}
  /\ phase' = "committed"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending, capacity>>

\* If any sector voted no, the transaction aborts and the write is discarded.
Abort ==
  /\ phase = "preparing"
  /\ \E p \in Sectors : votes[p] = "no"
  /\ phase' = "aborted"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, pending, record, committedLog, capacity>>

\* Close out a finished transaction and return the coordinator to idle.
Reset ==
  /\ phase \in {"committed", "aborted"}
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ pending' = None
  /\ votes' = [p \in Sectors |-> "none"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, committedLog, capacity>>

\* Runtime capacity change: any value from the committed count up to the max, so
\* capacity never drops below the allocations already committed.
ChangeCapacity ==
  /\ \E c \in Cardinality(record) .. MaxCap : capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, pending, record, committedLog>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Writes : Propose(w)
  \/ \E p \in Sectors, v \in {"yes", "no"} : Vote(p, v)
  \/ Commit
  \/ Abort
  \/ Reset
  \/ ChangeCapacity

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: every write that was ever acknowledged as committed is still
\* present in the shared record -- a commit is an append, never an overwrite.
NoLostUpdates == committedLog \subseteq record
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Sectors = {a1, a2}
  Writes = {w1, w2}
  None = None
  MaxCap = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CONSTRAINT CapConstraint
nl:
An air-traffic control system allocates runways and records each allocation in a
shared record using a two-phase commit protocol. A coordinator opens a
transaction by proposing an allocation write and asking every control sector to
vote. Each sector casts a single vote, yes or no, but may only vote yes while at
least one runway is still free within the current capacity. The coordinator
commits the transaction only if every sector has voted yes; on commit the write
is appended to the shared record and also recorded in a log of acknowledged
commits. If any sector votes no, the transaction aborts and its write is
discarded. After a transaction commits or aborts, the coordinator closes it out
and returns to idle, ready for the next proposal. The number of available
runways, the capacity, may change at runtime, but it never drops below the number
of allocations already committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: there are no lost updates -- every write that was ever acknowledged as committed remains present in the shared record, because a commit only appends to the record and never overwrites it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m0p0t5 ----
\* A network of vending machines contends for one critical shared resource (a
\* central cash-and-stock vault) using optimistic locking with retry. A machine
\* reads the vault's version stamp, then tries to enter the critical section;
\* entry succeeds only if the version is unchanged since the read, otherwise the
\* machine retries. Leaving the critical section bumps the version. A privileged
\* administrator may override and evict the current occupant. Throughout, the
\* vault is mutually exclusive: at most one machine is ever inside it.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, None, MaxVer

VARIABLES version, owner, mode, snapshot
vars == <<version, owner, mode, snapshot>>

VerBound == version <= MaxVer

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ owner = None
  /\ mode = [m \in Machines |-> "idle"]
  /\ snapshot = [m \in Machines |-> 0]

\* Optimistic read: take a snapshot of the current version stamp.
ReadVersion(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "idle"
  /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![m] = version]
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "reading"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner>>

\* Optimistic commit: enter the critical section only if the version is
\* unchanged since the read and the vault is free; become the recorded owner.
EnterCS(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "reading"
  /\ snapshot[m] = version
  /\ owner = None
  /\ owner' = m
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "critical"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snapshot>>

\* Conflict detected: the version moved since the read, so abandon and retry.
Retry(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "reading"
  /\ snapshot[m] # version
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, snapshot>>

\* Leave the critical section, releasing the vault and bumping its version.
LeaveCS(m) ==
  /\ mode[m] = "critical"
  /\ version < MaxVer
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED snapshot

\* Privileged administrator override: forcibly evict whoever holds the vault.
AdminEvict(m) ==
  /\ owner = m
  /\ owner' = None
  /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snapshot>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines : ReadVersion(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : EnterCS(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : Retry(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : LeaveCS(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines : AdminEvict(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion, tied to the shared owner field: a machine is inside the
\* critical section exactly when it is the vault's recorded owner. Since the
\* owner is a single value, at most one machine can be inside at any time.
MutualExclusion == \A m \in Machines : (mode[m] = "critical") <=> (owner = m)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
  Machines = {vm1, vm2}
  None = None
  MaxVer = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
CONSTRAINT VerBound
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one critical resource, a central
cash-and-stock vault, and coordinates access to it with optimistic locking and
retry. Each machine begins idle. To use the vault a machine first reads and
records the vault's current version stamp, entering a reading state. It then
attempts to enter the critical section, which succeeds only if the version stamp
is still the same as the one it read and the vault is currently free; on success
the machine becomes the vault's recorded owner and enters the critical section.
If instead the version stamp has changed since the read, the machine detects the
conflict, abandons the attempt, and returns to idle to retry. A machine leaves
the critical section by releasing the vault and bumping its version stamp. A
privileged administrator may override the protocol and forcibly evict whichever
machine currently holds the vault.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the vault is mutually exclusive -- a machine is inside the critical section exactly when it is the vault's recorded owner, so at most one machine is ever inside at the same time.

spec_text:
------------------------------ MODULE W4Od1m1p5t1 ------------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, Runways, None

VARIABLES holder, ring, committed, assignedBy, finalized, passes

vars == <<holder, ring, committed, assignedBy, finalized, passes>>

NextInRing(c) == ring[c]

Init ==
    /\ holder \in Controllers
    /\ ring \in [Controllers -> Controllers]
    /\ (\A c \in Controllers : ring[c] # c)
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ assignedBy = [w \in Runways |-> None]
    /\ finalized = {}
    /\ passes = {}

PostPass(c) ==
    /\ holder = c
    /\ passes' = passes \cup {[from |-> c, to |-> NextInRing(c)]}
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ring, committed, assignedBy, finalized>>

DeliverPass(m) ==
    /\ m \in passes
    /\ holder = None
    /\ holder' = m.to
    /\ passes' = passes \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ring, committed, assignedBy, finalized>>

Commit(c, w) ==
    /\ holder = c
    /\ w \notin committed
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {w}
    /\ assignedBy' = [assignedBy EXCEPT ![w] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ring, finalized, passes>>

Finalize(c, w) ==
    /\ holder = c
    /\ w \in committed
    /\ assignedBy[w] = c
    /\ w \notin finalized
    /\ finalized' = finalized \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, ring, committed, assignedBy, passes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : PostPass(c)
    \/ \E m \in passes : DeliverPass(m)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, w \in Runways : Commit(c, w)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, w \in Runways : Finalize(c, w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AssignmentSound ==
    /\ \A w \in Runways : (assignedBy[w] # None) <=> (w \in committed)
    /\ finalized \subseteq committed
    /\ \A w \in finalized : assignedBy[w] # None

================================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Runways = {w1, w2}
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AssignmentSound
nl:
An air-traffic control center coordinates several controllers who share responsibility for a small set of runways, and only the controller currently holding a circulating token may act. The token is passed around a fixed ring: the holder posts a hand-off message naming the next controller in the ring and immediately gives up the token. Because the control network reorders traffic, posted hand-off messages sit in an in-flight pool and may be delivered in any order, and a message is delivered only when nobody currently holds the token. The holder may irreversibly commit a runway assignment for any not-yet-assigned runway, recording itself as the committer; once committed a runway stays committed forever. The controller that committed a runway may later finalize it, a second one-way step that files the assignment permanently. Both committing and finalizing a runway are one-way actions that can each happen at most once per runway.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A runway records a committing controller exactly when it is committed, every finalized runway is also committed, and no finalized runway lacks a recorded committer, so assignments can never be filed out of order or duplicated.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m9p0t5 ----------------------------
\* Multiplayer lobby matchmaker: players compete for a single arena slot.
\* Reconfiguration bumps a monotone epoch; stale-epoch tokens are ignored.
\* A privileged admin may forcibly seize the slot for a player.
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, None

VARIABLES epoch, holder, grants, requests, adminSeized
vars == <<epoch, holder, grants, requests, adminSeized>>

MaxEpoch == 3

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ holder = None
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ adminSeized = FALSE

\* A player asks to join, tagging the request with the epoch it observed.
Request(p) ==
    /\ [player |-> p, epoch |-> epoch] \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {[player |-> p, epoch |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, grants, adminSeized>>

\* The slot must be free (no holder, no outstanding grant) to issue a token.
IssueGrant(r) ==
    /\ r \in requests
    /\ r.epoch = epoch
    /\ holder = None
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ grants' = {r}
    /\ requests' = requests \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, adminSeized>>

\* The token bearer enters the slot, consuming its grant.
Claim(g) ==
    /\ g \in grants
    /\ g.epoch = epoch
    /\ holder' = g.player
    /\ grants' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, requests, adminSeized>>

\* The current holder leaves the slot.
Release ==
    /\ holder # None
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grants, requests, adminSeized>>

\* Reconfigure the lobby: raise the epoch and discard all in-flight state.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ grants' = {}
    /\ requests' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED adminSeized

\* Admin override: forcibly hand the slot to a player, evicting cleanly.
AdminOverride(p) ==
    /\ ~adminSeized
    /\ holder' = p
    /\ grants' = {}
    /\ adminSeized' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, requests>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Players : Request(p)
    \/ \E r \in requests : IssueGrant(r)
    \/ \E g \in grants : Claim(g)
    \/ Release
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E p \in Players : AdminOverride(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: the slot never has both a seated holder and a live
\* grant token outstanding, so two players can never be admitted at once.
MutualExclusion == ~(holder # None /\ grants # {})
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {p1, p2}
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A matchmaker for a multiplayer game lobby hands out a single shared arena slot to competing players. Each player may submit a join request tagged with the epoch number it currently observes. When the slot is completely free (no seated holder and no outstanding grant), the matchmaker issues a grant token to one waiting request whose epoch is current. The player holding a valid grant token then claims the slot, becoming its holder, and later releases it when finished. To rebalance the lobby the coordinator can reconfigure, which raises the monotone epoch and discards every in-flight request and grant so that stale tokens are ignored. A privileged admin override can forcibly seize the slot for a chosen player, clearing any pending grant in the process. The whole point is that the slot behaves as a single critical resource.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The arena slot never simultaneously has a seated holder and a live grant token outstanding, so two players can never occupy the critical resource at the same time.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m6p3t2 ----------------------------
\* Car-wash conveyor line. Two independent controllers draw from one pool of
\* wash bays, handing each car a time-limited lease before it rolls onto a bay.
\* Leases expire; an expired bay may be re-leased, but never while occupied.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Controllers, Bays, Cars, None

VARIABLES clock, occupant, lease, requests, served
vars == <<clock, occupant, lease, requests, served>>

MaxClock == 2
LeaseLen == 2

\* A bay may be (re)leased when it holds no lease or its lease has expired.
Reusable(b) == IF lease[b] = None THEN TRUE ELSE lease[b].exp <= clock

\* A bay's lease is live (present and not yet expired).
Live(b) == lease[b] # None /\ lease[b].exp > clock

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ occupant = [b \in Bays |-> None]
    /\ lease = [b \in Bays |-> None]
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ served = {}

\* Either controller books a car for a bay by filing a request.
Submit(ctl, b, car) ==
    /\ [ctl |-> ctl, bay |-> b, car |-> car] \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {[ctl |-> ctl, bay |-> b, car |-> car]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, occupant, lease, served>>

\* A lease is granted only when the bay is free or its old lease has expired,
\* and the physical bay is empty -- the guard against double allocation.
GrantLease(r) ==
    /\ r \in requests
    /\ occupant[r.bay] = None
    /\ Reusable(r.bay)
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![r.bay] =
                    [car |-> r.car, ctl |-> r.ctl, exp |-> clock + LeaseLen]]
    /\ requests' = requests \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, occupant, served>>

\* A car with a live lease rolls onto its bay.
Admit(b) ==
    /\ Live(b)
    /\ occupant[b] = None
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![b] = lease[b].car]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, requests, served>>

\* Extend a live lease so a slow wash does not lapse mid-cycle.
Renew(b) ==
    /\ Live(b)
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b].exp = clock + LeaseLen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, occupant, requests, served>>

\* The car finishes, vacating the bay and clearing its lease.
Finish(b) ==
    /\ occupant[b] # None
    /\ served' = served \cup {occupant[b]}
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![b] = None]
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![b] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, requests>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxClock
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, lease, requests, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E ctl \in Controllers, b \in Bays, car \in Cars : Submit(ctl, b, car)
    \/ \E r \in requests : GrantLease(r)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Admit(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Renew(b)
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Finish(b)
    \/ Tick

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ClockBound == clock <= MaxClock

\* No double allocation: any physically occupied bay is backed by exactly the
\* car named in that bay's current lease, so no second car can share the bay.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A b \in Bays : occupant[b] # None =>
        (lease[b] # None /\ lease[b].car = occupant[b])
=============================================================================
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line runs several wash bays that are shared by two independent controllers drawing from one common pool. Either controller can file a request to book a particular car onto a particular bay. A controller grants a lease for a bay only when that bay is physically empty and its previous lease is absent or already expired, which is the guard that stops the two controllers from double-booking. Once a car holds a live lease it rolls onto its bay and becomes the occupant. A lease can be renewed while still live so a slow wash does not lapse in the middle of a cycle. When the car finishes it vacates the bay and its lease is cleared, and the car is recorded as served. A shared clock advances in bounded ticks, and expiry is measured against it. The design ensures a bay is never allocated to two cars at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every physically occupied bay is backed by exactly the car named in that bay's current lease, so the same slot is never allocated to two different cars simultaneously.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od10m1p5t0 ----------------------------
\* Subway signalling block system. Signal boxes sit on a token ring; only the
\* box holding the token may act on the track. Committing a block to a train
\* (routing it in) is irreversible and must happen at most once per block.
\* A signal box may silently drop offline and later come back.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Boxes, Blocks, None

VARIABLES holder, armed, fired, owner, crashed
vars == <<holder, armed, fired, owner, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ holder \in Boxes
    /\ armed = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]
    /\ fired = [b \in Blocks |-> FALSE]
    /\ owner = [b \in Blocks |-> None]
    /\ crashed = {}

\* The token holder clears (arms) a still-unrouted block, readying it.
Arm(b) ==
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ ~fired[b]
    /\ ~armed[b]
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, fired, owner, crashed>>

\* Irreversible commit: route a train into an armed block. Latches forever and
\* records the committing box; the block is disarmed and can never re-arm.
Commit(b) ==
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ armed[b]
    /\ ~fired[b]
    /\ fired' = [fired EXCEPT ![b] = TRUE]
    /\ armed' = [armed EXCEPT ![b] = FALSE]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![b] = holder]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

\* Pass the token round the ring to another live box.
PassToken ==
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ \E q \in Boxes : q # holder /\ holder' = q
    /\ UNCHANGED <<armed, fired, owner, crashed>>

\* A box silently crashes.
Crash(p) ==
    /\ p \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, armed, fired, owner>>

\* A crashed box recovers and rejoins the ring.
Recover(p) ==
    /\ p \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, armed, fired, owner>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Arm(b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Commit(b)
    \/ PassToken
    \/ \E p \in Boxes : Crash(p)
    \/ \E p \in Boxes : Recover(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* At-most-once: the irreversible commit is a latch tied to a recorded owner,
\* and a committed block can never be re-armed, so it can commit only once.
AtMostOnceCommit ==
    \A b \in Blocks :
        /\ (fired[b] <=> owner[b] # None)
        /\ (fired[b] => ~armed[b])
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Boxes = {s1, s2}
    Blocks = {blk1, blk2}
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOnceCommit
nl:
A subway signalling block system coordinates several signal boxes arranged on a token ring. Only the box currently holding the token is permitted to act on the track, which gives it exclusive access. The holder may arm a still-unrouted track block, clearing it and readying it for a train. The holder may then commit an armed block by routing a train into it; this commit is irreversible, latches permanently, and records which box performed it. Once committed, a block is disarmed and can never be armed again. The token is passed around the ring from the holder to another live box. Any signal box may silently crash and drop offline, and a crashed box may later recover and rejoin the ring. The central guarantee is that routing a train into a block is a one-shot action.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every track block the irreversible commit is a latch bound to a single recorded owner and can never be re-armed, so a train is routed into any given block at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m8p1t2 ----------------------------
\* University course-registration system. Two independent registrar instances
\* share one pool of course records. To update a record a registrar must take
\* the coarse catalog lock first, then the fine per-course lock (hierarchical),
\* read the current version, and only then commit -- so no update is lost.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Registrars, Records, None

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, version, rsnap, committers
vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, version, rsnap, committers>>

MaxVer == 4

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = None
    /\ fineLock = [r \in Records |-> None]
    /\ version = 0
    /\ rsnap = [g \in Registrars |-> None]
    /\ committers = {}

\* Take the coarse catalog lock (only one registrar may hold it).
AcquireCoarse(g) ==
    /\ coarseLock = None
    /\ coarseLock' = g
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, version, rsnap, committers>>

\* With the coarse lock held, take a fine per-course lock and snapshot version.
AcquireFine(g, r) ==
    /\ coarseLock = g
    /\ fineLock[r] = None
    /\ \A rr \in Records : fineLock[rr] # g
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = g]
    /\ rsnap' = [rsnap EXCEPT ![g] = version]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, version, committers>>

\* Commit the read-modify-write, bumping the version and releasing both locks.
Commit(g, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = g
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ coarseLock' = None
    /\ rsnap' = [rsnap EXCEPT ![g] = None]
    /\ committers' = committers \cup {g}

\* Abort a fine lock without writing.
ReleaseFine(g, r) ==
    /\ fineLock[r] = g
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![r] = None]
    /\ rsnap' = [rsnap EXCEPT ![g] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, version, committers>>

\* Drop the coarse lock (holding no fine locks).
ReleaseCoarse(g) ==
    /\ coarseLock = g
    /\ \A r \in Records : fineLock[r] # g
    /\ coarseLock' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, version, rsnap, committers>>

Next ==
    \/ \E g \in Registrars : AcquireCoarse(g)
    \/ \E g \in Registrars, r \in Records : AcquireFine(g, r)
    \/ \E g \in Registrars, r \in Records : Commit(g, r)
    \/ \E g \in Registrars, r \in Records : ReleaseFine(g, r)
    \/ \E g \in Registrars : ReleaseCoarse(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

VersionBound == version <= MaxVer

\* No lost updates: any registrar holding a fine lock (in its write section)
\* read the version that is still current, because the coarse lock it also
\* holds blocks every other commit -- so its write is never based on stale data.
NoLostUpdate ==
    \A g \in Registrars, r \in Records :
        fineLock[r] = g => rsnap[g] = version
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Registrars = {g1, g2}
    Records = {cs101, cs102}
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
CONSTRAINT VersionBound
nl:
A university course-registration system lets two independent registrar instances update a shared pool of course records. Because both instances touch the same pool, updates are protected by a two-level hierarchical lock. A registrar must first acquire the coarse catalog lock, of which only one may be held at a time. Holding the coarse lock, it then acquires a fine per-course lock on the record it wants and snapshots that record's current version. To finish it commits a read-modify-write that bumps the version and releases both locks together, recording itself as a committer. A registrar may instead abort by releasing the fine lock, and it drops the coarse lock once it holds no fine locks. Because the coarse lock serializes all commits, a registrar's snapshot stays current from read to write.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any registrar holding a fine lock read the version that is still current, so its committed update is never based on stale data and no update is ever lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m1p2t4 ----------------------------
\* Stock exchange opening auction. Traders sit on a token ring; only the token
\* holder may act on the order book. Shares flow through three stages -- a
\* trader's own holdings, resting orders in the book, and a crossed pool
\* awaiting settlement -- and no share is ever created or destroyed. The book's
\* resting capacity can be raised or lowered at runtime.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Traders, TotalShares, MaxCap

VARIABLES holder, holdings, book, crossed, capacity
vars == <<holder, holdings, book, crossed, capacity>>

\* Total shares currently held by all traders.
SumHoldings ==
    LET rec[S \in SUBSET Traders] ==
        IF S = {} THEN 0
        ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE
             IN holdings[x] + rec[S \ {x}]
    IN rec[Traders]

Init ==
    /\ holder \in Traders
    /\ holdings \in [Traders -> 0..TotalShares]
    /\ SumHoldings = TotalShares
    /\ book = 0
    /\ crossed = 0
    /\ capacity = 2

\* The token holder rests one of its shares as an order (bounded by capacity).
Submit(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ holdings[t] >= 1
    /\ book < capacity
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![t] = @ - 1]
    /\ book' = book + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crossed, capacity>>

\* The auction crosses one resting share into the pending-settlement pool.
Cross(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ book >= 1
    /\ book' = book - 1
    /\ crossed' = crossed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, holdings, capacity>>

\* A crossed share settles back into the token holder's holdings.
Settle(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ crossed >= 1
    /\ crossed' = crossed - 1
    /\ holdings' = [holdings EXCEPT ![t] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, book, capacity>>

\* Pass the token round the ring to another trader.
PassToken ==
    /\ \E q \in Traders : q # holder /\ holder' = q
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holdings, book, crossed, capacity>>

\* Raise the resting capacity of the book.
RaiseCap ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, holdings, book, crossed>>

\* Lower the resting capacity, but never below what is already resting.
LowerCap ==
    /\ capacity > book
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, holdings, book, crossed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Submit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Cross(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Settle(t)
    \/ PassToken
    \/ RaiseCap
    \/ LowerCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapBound == capacity <= MaxCap

\* Conservation: the shares scattered across holdings, resting orders, and the
\* crossed pool always sum to exactly the starting total -- nothing is created
\* or destroyed as shares flow through the auction.
SharesConserved == SumHoldings + book + crossed = TotalShares
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Traders = {t1, t2}
    TotalShares = 3
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SharesConserved
CONSTRAINT CapBound
nl:
A stock exchange opening auction matches shares among traders arranged on a token ring. Only the trader currently holding the token may act on the shared order book, which gives it exclusive access. Shares move through three stages: a trader's own holdings, resting orders sitting in the book, and a crossed pool of matched shares awaiting settlement. The token holder can submit one of its own shares as a resting order, provided the book has not reached its capacity. The auction crosses a resting share into the pending-settlement pool, and a crossed share later settles back into the token holder's holdings. The token is passed around the ring to another trader. The book's resting capacity can be raised at runtime up to a maximum, or lowered, but never below the number of shares already resting. Throughout, the shares merely change stage rather than appearing or vanishing.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shares spread across traders' holdings, resting orders, and the crossed pool always sum to exactly the starting total, so no share is ever created or destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m8p0t5 ----------------------------
\* Elevator bank in a skyscraper. A car may enter a hoistway shaft only by
\* taking the coarse dispatcher lock first and then a fine per-shaft lock
\* (hierarchical). A shaft is a critical resource: at most one car inside.
\* A privileged maintenance admin may override and seize a shaft.
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Shafts, Admin, None

Agents == Cars \cup {Admin}

VARIABLES coarseLock, fineLock, occupant, adminUsed, pending
vars == <<coarseLock, fineLock, occupant, adminUsed, pending>>

Init ==
    /\ coarseLock = None
    /\ fineLock = [s \in Shafts |-> None]
    /\ occupant = [s \in Shafts |-> None]
    /\ adminUsed = FALSE
    /\ pending = {}

\* A car signals that it wants to move.
Request(c) ==
    /\ c \notin pending
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, fineLock, occupant, adminUsed>>

\* Take the coarse dispatcher lock (only one car may hold it).
AcquireCoarse(c) ==
    /\ c \in pending
    /\ coarseLock = None
    /\ coarseLock' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, occupant, adminUsed, pending>>

\* Holding the coarse lock, take a free shaft's fine lock and enter it, then
\* drop the coarse lock. The shaft must be empty and unlocked to enter.
Enter(c, s) ==
    /\ coarseLock = c
    /\ fineLock[s] = None
    /\ occupant[s] = None
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ coarseLock' = None
    /\ pending' = pending \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED adminUsed

\* Give up the coarse lock without entering (e.g. no shaft available).
AbortCoarse(c) ==
    /\ coarseLock = c
    /\ coarseLock' = None
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineLock, occupant, adminUsed, pending>>

\* A car leaves its shaft, releasing the fine lock.
Exit(c, s) ==
    /\ occupant[s] = c
    /\ c \in Cars
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, adminUsed, pending>>

\* Admin override: forcibly seize a shaft for maintenance, evicting any car.
AdminOverride(s) ==
    /\ ~adminUsed
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = Admin]
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = Admin]
    /\ adminUsed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, pending>>

\* Admin releases a shaft it seized.
AdminRelease(s) ==
    /\ occupant[s] = Admin
    /\ occupant' = [occupant EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ fineLock' = [fineLock EXCEPT ![s] = None]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseLock, adminUsed, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Request(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : AcquireCoarse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, s \in Shafts : Enter(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : AbortCoarse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, s \in Shafts : Exit(c, s)
    \/ \E s \in Shafts : AdminOverride(s)
    \/ \E s \in Shafts : AdminRelease(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion: whatever agent physically occupies a shaft is exactly the
\* agent holding that shaft's fine lock, and a fine lock has one owner, so no
\* two cars can ever be inside the same shaft at once.
MutualExclusion ==
    \A s \in Shafts : occupant[s] # None => fineLock[s] = occupant[s]
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2}
    Shafts = {sh1, sh2}
    Admin = Admin
    None = None
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper coordinates several cars that share a set of hoistway shafts. Each shaft is a critical resource that at most one car may be inside at a time. A car that wants to move first files a request, then acquires the coarse dispatcher lock, of which only one car may be held at once. Holding the coarse lock, the car takes the fine lock on an empty, unlocked shaft, enters it, and immediately drops the coarse lock, keeping only the fine lock. If no shaft is available the car may abort and give up the coarse lock without entering. A car later exits its shaft, releasing the fine lock. A privileged maintenance admin may override the discipline to forcibly seize a shaft, evicting whatever car is inside, and later release it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Whatever agent physically occupies a shaft is exactly the agent holding that shaft's single-owner fine lock, so no two cars are ever inside the same shaft at once.
